implementerProof.how: Drove this round's three new claims myself rather than reading its tests, with a discriminator of my own: rememberWait returns before it touches the database when it has nothing to write, and reaches it when it has, so an outbox built on a pgxpool pointed at a port nothing listens on tells the two apart - no error means the gate refused to spend the notice, a dial failure naming the row means it set out to write the payload and the notice. On that rig (packages/daemon/internal/daemon, throwaway, deleted): only a wait spends the notice - Unmergeable, Armed and Merging do, while a GitHub read failure, a wrapped record-read failure, Refused and Removed do not; a stalled Lagging is a wait and permanentRefusal still holds it back; the wait is measured from the payload's Queued and not the row's created_at, so the reopen case (row two hours old, submission two minutes old) does not warn while the genuine hour does; a row already warned never sets out again; and the arm is still written whatever the cause. Separately, a pre-release payload {"number":42,"head":"ready-head","armed":true} decodes with Queued zero and validateOutboxPayload accepts it, so no stored row becomes unreadable, and omitzero keeps the key off the wire when the clock is zero. For the prompt and skill half I compared the clause in all three copies myself, diffed skills/legion-worker/SKILL.md against the bundle byte for byte, and ran check-dist with the negative control the implementer reports - a stale bundle is named and refused, exit 1 - then restored it. CI at the new code head d57679e9 I read on GitHub rather than re-running: ok internal/api 61.514s, internal/daemon 308.461s (272.799s under race), internal/record 16.438s, internal/workflow 139.023s, internal/prompts. The three merge-waiting tests it names exist in auto_merge_test.go and the reopen one asserts what it claims, including the second notice naming 1h2m0s. One number in its handoff is off: it reports 57 insertions and 0 deletions for the docs/solutions notes, and jj diff --stat over docs/solutions reports 45 insertions and 0 deletions across five files. The 'additions only' claim holds; the count does not.

Both are imperatives addressed to a worker, not narration of a dated run, so both fall under the architect's rule. Neither is dead text: the INFRA-117 learning is `status: active`, dated 2026-10-22, `module: legion-worker`, and is the newest learning about a base with no required check - the exposure this change leaves to GitHub; the external-red learning's frontmatter marks only its section 3 superseded (by LEGION-631), and the quoted instruction stands. `skill://legion-oracle` sends every agent to docs/solutions before it works, and the spec's own proof for deliverable two is 'a search of the whole tree finds no CI line left to write'.

Why they survived is the issue's own defect shape, which is why this is a failure rather than a note. The fix's search was `grep -rln 'CI:' docs/solutions`, the literal with a colon; `grep -c 'CI:'` on both files returns 0, because both write 'CI line' without it. Seven hits were found, five superseded and two correctly judged as prose (docs/solutions/testing/a-container-build-inside-go-test-spends-the-tests-deadline.md:92 'Measured in CI: ...' and .../a-held-clock-test-...-LEGION-694.md:37 '`-race` runs nowhere but CI:'). The rule was applied correctly to every hit the search returned; the search was narrower than the rule, and its result looked complete.

Remedy: a `**Superseded 2026-10-23 (dispatch://INFRA-83):**` paragraph on each, in the shape the five already carry, as an addition. A third text is borderline and the architect's call, not mine to decide: docs/solutions/legion/the-pull-request-body-is-shared-by-every-role-edit-the-live-body-by-section-never-overwrite-it-from-a-local-copy.md:41 says 'a tester or reviewer appending its line must edit the live body too - the implementer's `CI` line may already name a newer head after a conflict-forced rebase'. Its instruction (edit the live body) still holds; only the reason it gives is stale, so by the rule as written it is not an instruction to write the deleted line.

No red test pins this one, and the reason is the plan's own D8: the repository rejected a standing text test over the tree's markdown because it would lock prose that will legitimately be rewritten, and the idiom it chose instead is the composed-prompt retired-phrase list plus a recorded sweep. A narrow test would also fire on the five supersedes notes themselves, each of which contains the string `CI:` line while saying it no longer exists. The evidence is therefore the command and its output above, which reproduce in one line.
